idea.en: Find the parasternal long axis from the left sternal edge without help.

caption.en: Echo Lab render of the Parasternal long axis. Match this plane on the simulator, then find it on a patient.

note.en: Landmarks to confirm: Cavity of left ventricle

steps.en: What you see: The left ventricle lies across the screen with the interventricular septum in the near field and the posterior wall in the far field. Behind the ventricle sit the mitral valve and the left atrium, while the aortic root with its open cusps rises from the front of the ventricle toward the ascending aorta.
Landmarks to confirm: Do not accept the view until each of these is on screen.
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Each mistake below comes from the view catalogue with its correction.
Normal values: Left ventricular internal diameter at end diastole: 42 to 58 mm in men, 38 to 52 mm in women.
Septal and posterior wall thickness at end diastole: 6 to 10 mm in men, 6 to 9 mm in women.
Left ventricular ejection fraction: 55 percent or more is normal, below 30 percent is severely reduced.
Measure diameters at end diastole with the leading edge to leading edge method.

Pitfalls: A gap in the mid septum seen only in this view is almost always dropout, so confirm any suspected defect in the short axis before reporting it. Pericardial fluid collects behind the posterior wall first, while pleural fluid continues past the descending aorta, so find the aorta before calling an effusion.

Indian context: Rheumatic heart disease is common in India, so inspect the mitral leaflets here in every young adult with breathlessness. Thickened tips with diastolic doming of the anterior leaflet point to rheumatic mitral stenosis long before the gradient rises.

analogy.en: Landmarks to confirm: Cavity of left ventricle

spot.en: Landmarks to confirm: Cavity of left ventricle
Non coronary cusp of aortic valve
Right coronary cusp of aortic valve

Common mistakes and how to correct them: Foreshortened left ventricle with a rounded apex that hides the true apex. Correct it by sliding toward the apex until the ventricle is at its longest and the apex tapers to a point.

Septal dropout from an off axis cut that mimics a septal defect. Correct it by rocking the probe slightly and lowering the gain until the septum reads as one continuous bright line through the whole cycle.
Probe slid too medial so the right ventricle looks larger than the left ventricle. Correct it by sliding back toward the sternum until the right ventricle is a small triangle at the top of the image.

todo.en: How to get it: Place the probe at left sternal edge, third or fourth intercostal space.
Point the probe marker toward the right shoulder, about ten o clock.
If ribs block the window, slide one space down and ask the patient to breathe out and hold. Keep the septum near horizontal, since a steep septum means you have slid too far toward the apex.
Freeze the image only when every listed landmark is on screen at once.

remember.en: Spot foreshortening and dropout before they mislead you.

q.en: Where do you place the probe for the parasternal long axis?

o.en: Left sternal edge, third or fourth rib space
Suprasternal notch with the neck extended

why.en: The parasternal window sits at the left sternal edge in the third or fourth space.

q.en: Which wall lies in the near field in the parasternal long axis?

why.en: The septum is the near field wall and the posterior wall is the far field wall.

q.en: A bright gap in the mid septum shows only in this view. What next?

o.en: Confirm in the short axis since dropout is likely
Start colour Doppler of the aorta

why.en: Septal dropout is common in the long axis, so a defect needs a second plane.
